Validate Weight Outlier Methods with Artificial Errors

Source: R/validate.R
validate_outliers.Rd

Add artificial errors to body weight records that passed the checks, then run clean_weight() with each outlier method and measure how many artificial errors are found, how many good records are removed, and how far ADG moves from the ADG of the clean records.

validate_outliers(
  visits,
  qc = qc_config(),
  methods = list(track = "track", rlm = "rlm", loess = "loess", stl = "stl", sd = "sd",
    `stl+rlm+sd` = c("stl", "rlm", "sd")),
  rate = 0.05,
  size = c(3, 15),
  direction = c("both", "down", "up"),
  reps = 3,
  max_pigs = NULL,
  seed = 1,
  verbose = 1,
  cores = 1
)

Arguments

visits

Result of prep_visits().

qc

QC settings from qc_config(). They define the clean records (records kept by qc) and every setting except weight_outlier.

methods

Named list of outlier method sets to compare; each element is a value for weight_outlier (run without tracking), or "track" for the tracking from the end of the test (weight_track = TRUE).

rate

Share of clean records that receive an artificial error. Default 0.05.

size

Range of the error size in kg. Default c(3, 15).

direction

"both" (default): errors are added or subtracted at random; "down": weights too low only (pig partly on the scale); "up": too high only (two pigs on the scale).

reps

Number of repetitions. Default 3.

max_pigs

Use a random sample of at most this many pigs, to save time on large data (a few hundred pigs are enough). Default NULL: all.

seed

Random seed, for reproducible results.

verbose

0 (silent), 1 (summary and progress, default).

cores

Number of CPU cores for clean_weight() and calc_adg().

Value

A list of class ppt_validation with

  • summary: one row per method: sensitivity (share of artificial errors found), false_positive_rate (share of clean records removed), precision, adg_bias and adg_rmse (g/d, against the ADG of the clean records), adg_spearman (rank correlation) and n_pigs;

  • per_rep: the same for each repetition;

  • settings.

Details

The clean records are those that qc keeps, so they are not free of error themselves. A method that disagrees with qc therefore gets a higher false_positive_rate; compare methods mainly on sensitivity and ADG. The row none shows the result when only weight_range is applied (errors that push a weight outside it are still found).

Errors placed at random times shift single records but hardly move a growth curve fitted to hundreds of records, so ADG differences between methods are small; they mostly reflect which good records each method removes.

Examples

visits <- prep_visits(nedap, verbose = 0)
w <- clean_weight(visits, verbose = 0)

# 1. weight outlier methods: 5% artificial errors of 3-15 kg
vo <- validate_outliers(visits, reps = 1)
#> 
#> ── Validating weight outlier methods (1 repetition, 5% artificial errors) ──────
#> Validating outlier methods ■■■■■■■■■■                        29% | ETA:  4s
#> Validating outlier methods ■■■■■■■■■■■■■■                    43% | ETA:  3s

#> loess: 89% of errors found, 1.2% of good records removed, ADG error 1.7 g/d
